title: Kingdom of Burundi
description: By tradition the state is founded by Cambarantama; the kingdom ruled by a mwami and a princely caste will survive into the twentieth century.

title: First European contacts
description: European explorers and missionaries begin to make brief visits to the kingdom, which they compare in organisation to the states of ancient Greece.

title: Part of German East Africa
description: Burundi becomes part of German East Africa; King Mwezi IV Gisabo resists European influence and must eventually concede German suzerainty.

title: UN trust territory
description: Ruanda-Urundi, under Belgian administration since the First World War, becomes a United Nations trust territory meant to be prepared for independence.

title: UPRONA founded
description: Prince Louis Rwagasore founds the Union for National Progress, the multi-ethnic party that leads the drive for independence.

title: Mwambutsa requests independence
description: King Mwambutsa IV asks Belgium for independence and the separation of Burundi from Rwanda.

title: First elections
description: UPRONA wins over four-fifths of the vote in Burundi's first elections, making Prince Rwagasore prime minister designate.

title: Rwagasore assassinated
description: A gunman kills Prince Louis Rwagasore weeks after his election victory, robbing Burundi of its most popular nationalist leader.

title: Independence
description: Burundi becomes independent of Belgium as a constitutional monarchy under King Mwambutsa IV.

title: Ngendandumwe assassinated
description: The Hutu prime minister Pierre Ngendandumwe is killed days after taking office, setting off revolts and repression along ethnic lines.

title: Micombero coup
description: Captain Michel Micombero deposes King Ntare V, abolishes the monarchy and declares a military republic.

title: Ikiza
description: After a Hutu rising in the south, the Tutsi-dominated state kills well over a hundred thousand Hutu by the end of August, including nearly every educated Hutu.

title: Bagaza coup
description: Colonel Jean-Baptiste Bagaza takes power in a bloodless coup and rules through a Tutsi-dominated military regime.

title: Buyoya coup
description: Major Pierre Buyoya overthrows Bagaza and suspends the constitution.

title: Ntega and Marangara massacres
description: The army puts down Hutu unrest in two northern communes; thousands are killed and tens of thousands flee to Rwanda.

title: Ndadaye elected
description: Melchior Ndadaye beats Buyoya in the first free presidential election and becomes the country's first Hutu head of state.

title: Ndadaye assassinated
description: Tutsi soldiers kill President Ndadaye after barely three months in office, and the civil war that follows lasts twelve years and kills about 300,000 people.

title: Buyoya returns
description: Pierre Buyoya seizes power again, and neighbouring states answer with economic sanctions.

title: Arusha agreement
description: The government, parliament and opposition sign a power-sharing peace deal, though the main Hutu rebel groups fight on for now.

title: Nkurunziza becomes president
description: Former rebel leader Pierre Nkurunziza is sworn in after his CNDD-FDD sweeps the post-war elections.

title: Joins the East African Community
description: Burundi and Rwanda are admitted as full members of the revived East African Community.

title: Coup attempt
description: Weeks into protests against Nkurunziza's third-term bid, a general declares a coup while the president is abroad; it fails within two days.

title: Constitutional referendum
description: Voters approve constitutional changes that lengthen presidential terms, though Nkurunziza then says he will not run again.
